_note: Additions to dictionary entries that come from us rather than from a corpus.
The Igbo corpus reaches 12,291 published headwords but only 4,805 of them carry an
example sentence, and 1,120 of those hold eight or more while 7,486 hold none — the
sentences are concentrated on the words the corpora happened to illustrate. Some
entries also carry a single gloss where the word has several senses (bilie was
'rose' and nothing else), because a source gave one sense and the importer records
what the source said.
WHY THIS IS A FILE
Same reason as data/names/origins.json and the owner's corrections: it is OUR
knowledge, so it is tracked in git and reviewable, unlike everything under
data/sources/. And because the corpora are re-imported whenever a source is added,
an addition that lives only in the database is an addition that can be lost without
anyone noticing.
WHAT THESE ARE, HONESTLY
Meanings here are senses the word has that no imported source stated. Examples are
written by Ozikoro, not quoted from a publication, and they are attributed to an
editorial source rather than to a book that never printed them. They are drafts for
the owner to correct — a wrong example is worse than no example, so each one is
kept short, built from the word's plainest sense, and easy to replace.
Fields: headword (required), meanings[] (added to the entry, never replacing what a
